title: Testicular Torsion: Signs, Timing and Diagnostic Pitfalls
subject: Surgical Triads
preview: Testicular torsion causes acute scrotal pain and can rapidly threaten testicular viability.
quickRevision: Testicular torsion causes acute scrotal pain and can rapidly threaten testicular viability.
High clinical suspicion demands urgent urological evaluation; ultrasound should not delay exploration when torsion is likely.
Epididymitis may have a different onset and infective features, but overlap prevents diagnosis by one sign alone.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Testicular torsion causes acute scrotal pain and can rapidly threaten testicular viability.
High-riding testis or absent cremasteric reflex may support suspicion, but neither is universally present.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: High clinical suspicion demands urgent urological evaluation; ultrasound should not delay exploration when torsion is likely.
Epididymitis may have a different onset and infective features, but overlap prevents diagnosis by one sign alone.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not reassure a patient solely because pain has intermittently improved; intermittent torsion occurs.
